title: "GAM: infection by body size"
format:
  html:
    toc: true
df-print: kable
---

Purpose: a finer-resolution, qualitative companion to stage 1 for species in the discussion. Per
species, prevalence and load are modeled as a smooth function of SVL (plus a metamorph
baseline), rather than as a two-level subadult - adult contrast. Specification and reasons:
`README.md` "Downstream models" -> "GAM". Replaces `size_bd_gam/02_size_bd_GAM_modeling.qmd`
(m3: m11g climate priors, stage-specific random effects; kept until retired).

In short:

- **same as the stage 1 model of each species**: response (`bd_load_co100_density`, hurdle
  lognormal), the nuisance intercepts (site, site-year, event), which of them a part keeps (the
  R2 / R3 flags of `01_contrast_species.csv`, reused as they are, not recomputed), and the
  nuisance priors
- **different by design**: metamorphs are included, and SVL enters as a thin plate smooth in
  place of the stage term `stage_c`. There is no stage term and no varying size effect: whether
  the subadult - adult difference varies across sites, years or events is stage 1's question
  (Q2-Q4)
- **no climate terms**: the event intercepts absorb weather shared by all animals in an event
- **species**: the 14 species with >= 100 swabs of each stage (adult, subadult) in the stage 1
  data. A post-hoc description of the existing GAM data set (`size_bd_gam/00`, chosen by hand
  for SVL coverage): every species in it has >= 130, every other stage 1 species <= 97
  (*A. americanus*). Other species can be added by name if the discussion needs them (with data
  prep in `size_bd_gam/00`), labeled as below the cutoff
- **how informed a curve is** follows stage 1: comparisons between events are down-weighted by
  the event intercepts, not discarded (random, not fixed, effects), so a species' curve is about
  as informed as its stage 1 contrast, with the same caveats (tier, time-segregated flag). These
  are carried in the species table, for choosing which curves to show

Run order: this script (fits locally, then fit health and prior sensitivity) ->
`07_gam_analysis.Rmd` (curves, figures, manuscript exports).

# Setup

```{r}
#| output: false
librarian::shelf(tidyverse, here, brms, cmdstanr, posterior)

# event definition (event_ids), response_col and the R2 constant come from stage 1, so the GAM
# cannot drift from it
source(here("size_bd_contrast", "contrast_data_functions.R"))
# formula and prior builders, run settings (copied verbatim into the cluster script)
source(here("size_bd_contrast", "gam_model_functions.R"))
# subadult / adult svl cutoffs, for the species table
source(here("size_bd_unified", "svl_stage_cutoffs.R"))

intermediates_dir = here("size_bd_contrast", "intermediates")
models_dir = here("size_bd_contrast", "models")

set_cmdstan_path(Sys.getenv("cmd_stan_path"))
```

# Data

```{r}
# GAM data (size_bd_gam/00-01): stage 1 sources and populations, plus metamorphs and SVL bounds
# per species. life_stage_simple is metamorph / subadult / adult; is_not_metamorph = 1 for
# subadults and adults. the climate columns in it are not used.
load(here("size_bd_gam", "intermediates", "brms_data_gam_2026-11-15.RData"))
gam_data_raw = brms_data
rm(brms_data)

# stage 1 species table: counts, tiers, nuisance flags (R2 / R3), co-sampling, time-segregated flag
stage1_species = read_csv(file.path(intermediates_dir, "01_contrast_species.csv"),
                          show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  filter(include)
```

## Species

```{r}
# inclusion: >= 100 swabs of each stage in the stage 1 data (set 2026-11-27, post hoc; see the
# header). stage 1 counts, not GAM counts: the GAM's staging reassigns small animals to
# metamorphs (e.g. r. sierrae 2873 GAM vs 4194 stage 1 subadults), and stage 1 is the shared
# reference
gam_min_stage_swabs = 100

gam_species = stage1_species %>%
  filter(pmin(n_adult, n_subadult) >= gam_min_stage_swabs) %>%
  pull(taxon_capture) %>%
  sort()

# every selected species must be in the GAM data (a species added to the cutoff needs data prep
# in size_bd_gam/00 first)
missing_gam = setdiff(gam_species, unique(gam_data_raw$taxon_capture))
if (length(missing_gam) > 0) stop("Not in the GAM data: ", paste(missing_gam, collapse = ", "))

gam_species
```

## Events and grouping columns

```{r}
# events as in stage 1 (event_ids: no gap > 5 days, runs > 14 days split at their longest gap),
# per species x population. the one difference: the dates are all of the species' swab dates,
# metamorphs included, so a metamorph-only survey is its own event and one shared with adults
# joins theirs. event counts can therefore differ slightly from stage 1.
# add_contrast_groups() is not reused: it recodes life_stage_simple to adult / subadult, which
# would turn metamorphs into NA.
add_gam_groups = function(df) {
  events = df %>%
    distinct(taxon_capture, population, date) %>%
    arrange(taxon_capture, population, date) %>%
    group_by(taxon_capture, population) %>%
    mutate(event_k = event_ids(as.numeric(date))) %>%
    ungroup()

  df %>%
    left_join(events, by = c("taxon_capture", "population", "date")) %>%
    mutate(pop_year = paste(population, year, sep = "_"),
           pop_year_event = paste(population, year, event_k, sep = "_"))
}

gam_data = gam_data_raw %>%
  filter(taxon_capture %in% gam_species) %>%
  add_gam_groups()

# saved for 07 (curves over the data each model was fit to, manuscript export)
saveRDS(gam_data, file.path(intermediates_dir, "06_gam_model_data.rds"))

gam_data %>%
  group_by(taxon_capture) %>%
  summarise(n_swabs = n(),
            n_metamorph = sum(life_stage_simple == "metamorph"),
            n_populations = n_distinct(population),
            n_site_years = n_distinct(pop_year),
            n_events = n_distinct(pop_year_event))
```

# Model

## Formula and priors

`gam_formula()` and `gam_priors()` are in `gam_model_functions.R` (shared with the cluster
script). Per part (mu, hu):

- size: metamorph baseline (the intercept) + `s(svl_mm, by = is_not_metamorph)`, a thin plate
  smooth over subadults and adults; `s(svl_mm)` for species without metamorphs
- nuisance: `(1 | population)`, plus `(1 | pop_year)` and `(1 | pop_year_event)` where stage 1
  kept them for that part (R2); sigma by population where stage 1's is (R3)
- priors: stage 1's nuisance priors (intercepts, intercept sds, sigma); smooth terms at brms'
  defaults

## Species table

```{r}
# what each curve rests on, for choosing which to show (07) and for the caveats: stage 1 counts,
# positives, tier, co-sampling, time-segregated flag and stage 1 contrast support, next to the
# GAM's own counts and structure. written before fitting so it exists without the fits.
stage1_support = read_csv(file.path(intermediates_dir, "03_contrast_species_summary.csv"),
                          show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  filter(variant == "main") %>%
  select(taxon_capture, part, contrast_median, contrast_support) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = part, values_from = c(contrast_median, contrast_support))

gam_structure = gam_data %>%
  group_by(taxon_capture) %>%
  summarise(gam_n_metamorph = sum(life_stage_simple == "metamorph"),
            gam_n_subadult = sum(life_stage_simple == "subadult"),
            gam_n_adult = sum(life_stage_simple == "adult"),
            gam_n_events = n_distinct(pop_year_event),
            svl_term = if_else(gam_n_metamorph > 0, "s(svl_mm, by = is_not_metamorph)", "s(svl_mm)"))

gam_species_table = stage1_species %>%
  filter(taxon_capture %in% gam_species) %>%
  select(taxon_capture, n_adult, n_subadult, n_pos_adult, n_pos_subadult,
         n_co_event, n_co_load_event, n_co_popyear, n_co_pop,
         tier_hu, tier_mu, flag_time_segregated,
         hu_has_pop_year, hu_has_event, mu_has_pop_year, mu_has_event, sigma_by_population) %>%
  left_join(stage1_support, by = "taxon_capture") %>%
  left_join(gam_structure, by = "taxon_capture") %>%
  left_join(svl_cutoff_species(gam_species) %>% select(taxon_capture, svl_cutoff_mm = svl_mm_cutoff),
            by = "taxon_capture")

write_csv(gam_species_table, file.path(intermediates_dir, "06_gam_species.csv"))

(gam_species_table_summary = gam_species_table %>%
  select(taxon_capture, n_adult, n_subadult, n_co_event, tier_hu, tier_mu,
         flag_time_segregated, contrast_support_prevalence, contrast_support_load))
```

## Structure check

```{r}
# formula and prior for each species, without fitting: make_standata builds the data Stan would
# get (fails on a formula error), validate_prior fails on a prior that matches no parameter
gam_model_file = function(sp) file.path(models_dir, gam_model_name(sp))

gam_setup = function(sp) {
  sp_row = filter(gam_species_table, taxon_capture == sp)
  model_data = gam_data %>% filter(taxon_capture == sp) %>% droplevels()
  list(formula = gam_formula(sp_row, model_data),
       prior = gam_priors(sp_row),
       data = model_data)
}

structure_check = map(gam_species, function(sp) {
  s = gam_setup(sp)
  sdata = make_standata(s$formula, data = s$data, family = hurdle_lognormal(), prior = s$prior)
  validate_prior(s$prior, s$formula, data = s$data, family = hurdle_lognormal())
  tibble(taxon_capture = sp,
         mu = deparse1(s$formula$formula),
         hu = deparse1(s$formula$pforms$hu),
         sigma = deparse1(s$formula$pforms$sigma),
         n_obs = sdata$N)
}) %>%
  list_rbind()

structure_check
```

# Timing test

```{r}
#| eval: false
# short runs to size the cluster jobs (r-brms-contained/hpc/run_size_bd_contrast_gam_modeling.sbatch),
# extrapolated as in 02: slowest chain, warmup x 2000/300, sampling x 2000/100 (production:
# 2000 warmup + 2000 sampling per chain). three species spanning size and structure:
#   silverstoneia_flotator   n ~600,  no metamorphs, s(svl_mm)
#   rana_catesbeiana         n ~1.9k, metamorphs, by-smooth
#   rana_clamitans           n ~2.7k, metamorphs, by-smooth
# the larger species are extrapolated from these with run time ~ n^b: b from the three runs,
# bounded by 1.2 (stage 1's observed growth) and 1.6 (the upper bound assumed in 02). confirm
# with the first cluster runs (sacct Elapsed, MaxRSS).
timing_species = c("silverstoneia_flotator", "rana_catesbeiana", "rana_clamitans")

timing_results = map(timing_species, function(sp) {
  s = gam_setup(sp)
  start = Sys.time()
  fit = brm(formula = s$formula, data = s$data, family = hurdle_lognormal(), prior = s$prior,
            control = list(adapt_delta = gam_adapt_delta, max_treedepth = gam_max_treedepth),
            chains = gam_n_chains, iter = 400, warmup = 300,
            seed = 128, cores = gam_n_chains, backend = "cmdstanr", refresh = 0)
  chain_times = rstan::get_elapsed_time(fit$fit)
  np = nuts_params(fit)
  tibble(taxon_capture = sp,
         n = nrow(s$data),
         total_min = as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), start, units = "mins")),  # incl. compilation
         max_chain_warmup_s = max(chain_times[, "warmup"]),
         max_chain_sample_s = max(chain_times[, "sample"]),
         est_production_h = (max(chain_times[, "warmup"]) * (gam_n_warmup / 300) +
                               max(chain_times[, "sample"]) * ((gam_n_iter - gam_n_warmup) / 100)) / 3600,
         divergences = sum(np$Value[np$Parameter == "divergent__"]))
}) %>%
  list_rbind()

timing_results

# growth exponent from the three runs, and the extrapolation to every species from the largest
# timed one (r. clamitans) at that exponent and at the 1.2 / 1.6 bounds
b_fit = unname(coef(lm(log(est_production_h) ~ log(n), data = timing_results))[2])
ref = slice_max(timing_results, n)

timing_extrapolated = gam_species_table %>%
  transmute(taxon_capture, array_index = match(taxon_capture, sort(gam_species)) - 1,
            n = gam_n_adult + gam_n_subadult + gam_n_metamorph) %>%
  mutate(est_h_fit = ref$est_production_h * (n / ref$n)^b_fit,
         est_h_1.2 = ref$est_production_h * (n / ref$n)^1.2,
         est_h_1.6 = ref$est_production_h * (n / ref$n)^1.6) %>%
  arrange(n)

b_fit
timing_extrapolated
```

# Fit

```{r}
#| eval: false
# local fits, one per species. or on the cluster: r-brms-contained/size_bd_contrast_gam_modeling.R
# (same builders and settings), then copy models/size_bd_contrast_gam/*.rds into
# size_bd_contrast/models/; this chunk then loads them instead of refitting.
# brm(file = ...) saves the fit and, when the file exists, loads it (file_refit = "never");
# delete a file to refit it.
# no LOO: the curves are read qualitatively and no models are compared.
# the event intercepts add one parameter per event and part: r. sierrae (997 events) and
# r. muscosa are the long runs.
fit_gam = function(sp) {
  s = gam_setup(sp)
  cat("Fitting GAM for:", sp, "\n")
  brm(formula = s$formula,
      data = s$data,
      family = hurdle_lognormal(),
      prior = s$prior,
      control = list(adapt_delta = gam_adapt_delta, max_treedepth = gam_max_treedepth),
      chains = gam_n_chains, iter = gam_n_iter, warmup = gam_n_warmup,
      seed = gam_seed, cores = gam_n_chains, backend = "cmdstanr",
      file = gam_model_file(sp), file_refit = "never")
}

# small species first; r. sierrae last
fit_order = gam_species_table %>%
  arrange(gam_n_adult + gam_n_subadult + gam_n_metamorph) %>%
  pull(taxon_capture)

walk(fit_order, fit_gam)
```

# Fit health

```{r}
#| eval: false
# divergences, max rhat, min bulk / tail ess per fit (summarise_draws over all parameters,
# random effects included)
gam_fit_health = map(gam_species, function(sp) {
  fit = readRDS(paste0(gam_model_file(sp), ".rds"))
  np = nuts_params(fit)
  dr = summarise_draws(as_draws_array(fit), "rhat", "ess_bulk", "ess_tail")
  tibble(taxon_capture = sp,
         n_divergent = sum(np$Value[np$Parameter == "divergent__"]),
         max_treedepth_hits = sum(np$Value[np$Parameter == "treedepth__"] >= 12),
         max_rhat = max(dr$rhat, na.rm = TRUE),
         min_ess_bulk = min(dr$ess_bulk, na.rm = TRUE),
         min_ess_tail = min(dr$ess_tail, na.rm = TRUE))
}) %>%
  list_rbind()

write_csv(gam_fit_health, file.path(intermediates_dir, "06_gam_fit_health.csv"))
gam_fit_health
```

# Prior sensitivity

```{r}
#| eval: false
library(priorsense)

# power-scaling (as in 02, "Prior sensitivity"): how much the posterior of each variance term
# moves when the prior is weakened or strengthened. cjs_dist > 0.05 = the prior matters.
#   sds_*  smooth wiggliness (how far the SVL curve may bend); student_t(3, 0, 2.5) default
#   sd_*   nuisance intercept sds (site, site-year, event); exponential(1)
# a wiggliness sd that is prior-shaped means the data say little about the curve's shape beyond
# its linear part: read the curve's bends with that in mind.
gam_powerscale = map(gam_species, function(sp) {
  fit = readRDS(paste0(gam_model_file(sp), ".rds"))
  vars = grep("^(sds|sd)_", variables(fit), value = TRUE)
  powerscale_sensitivity(fit, variable = vars) %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    mutate(taxon_capture = sp, .before = 1)
}) %>%
  list_rbind()

write_csv(gam_powerscale, file.path(intermediates_dir, "06_gam_powerscale.csv"))

gam_powerscale %>%
  filter(diagnosis != "-")
```
